Navigation

Purpose: move between pages and places. Every pattern here is real

Purpose: move between pages and places. Every pattern here is real links in semantic landmarks — never buttons pretending to navigate, never action menus pretending to be navigation.

Patterns

Navbar — brand + link group + optional actions:

<header class="sq-navbar">
  <div class="sq-container sq-navbar__inner">
    <a class="sq-navbar__brand" href="/">Harbor Notes</a>
    <nav aria-label="Primary">
      <ul class="sq-nav">
        <li><a class="sq-nav__link" href="/articles">Articles</a></li>
        <li>
          <a class="sq-nav__link" href="/about" aria-current="page">About</a>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </div>
</header>

Collapsible mobile nav — <details class="sq-nav-menu" open> wraps the link list; below 48rem it toggles behind a "Menu" summary, at 48rem+ the summary hides and links show inline. Zero JavaScript:

<nav aria-label="Primary">
  <details class="sq-nav-menu" open>
    <summary>Menu</summary>
    <ul class="sq-nav">
      <li><a class="sq-nav__link" href="/articles">Articles</a></li>
    </ul>
  </details>
</nav>

The open attribute is load-bearing, not a default to strip: closed <details> content stays hidden from assistive technology even when CSS displays it, so removing open would show links to sighted users at wide viewports while hiding them from screen readers. Default-open keeps both trees in agreement at every width; mobile users collapse with one toggle.

Breadcrumbs — ordered trail; separators are CSS (never announced); the current page is plain text with aria-current="page":

<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol class="sq-breadcrumbs">
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/articles">Articles</a></li>
    <li aria-current="page">The 64-pixel rule</li>
  </ol>
</nav>

Pagination — page navigation with rel, visible prev/next labels, current page as text:

<nav aria-label="Articles pages">
  <ul class="sq-pagination">
    <li><a href="/articles?p=1" rel="prev">← Newer</a></li>
    <li><a href="/articles?p=1">1</a></li>
    <li aria-current="page">2</li>
    <li><a href="/articles?p=3">3</a></li>
    <li><a href="/articles?p=3" rel="next">Older →</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

Sidebar — vertical nav column; stacks above content on narrow, sticky beside it at 64rem+:

<div class="sq-with-sidebar">
  <nav class="sq-sidebar sq-sidebar--sticky" aria-label="Docs">
    <p class="sq-sidebar__title">Guides</p>
    <ul class="sq-nav sq-nav--vertical">
      <li>
        <a class="sq-nav__link" href="/docs" aria-current="page">Start</a>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
  <div><!-- content --></div>
</div>

Stepper — progressive flow (checkout, onboarding). Active step is aria-current="step", finished steps take --done; empty markers print their DOM position automatically:

<ol class="sq-stepper">
  <li class="sq-stepper__step sq-stepper__step--done">
    <span class="sq-stepper__marker" aria-hidden="true">
      <svg
        class="sq-icon sq-icon--small"
        viewBox="0 0 24 24"
        fill="none"
        stroke="currentColor"
        stroke-width="2"
        stroke-linecap="round"
        stroke-linejoin="round"
        focusable="false"
      >
        <path d="m5 12 5 5 9-11" />
      </svg>
    </span>
    <span class="sq-stepper__label">Delivery window</span>
  </li>
  <li class="sq-stepper__step" aria-current="step">
    <span class="sq-stepper__marker"></span>
    <span class="sq-stepper__label">Address</span>
  </li>
  <li class="sq-stepper__step">
    <span class="sq-stepper__marker"></span>
    <span class="sq-stepper__label">Payment</span>
  </li>
</ol>

The stepper is a status display, not an interactive control: steps are list items, never buttons or links to click themselves into place. The form that drives the flow does the navigating. Steps go vertical below 48rem and horizontal at 48rem+ (connectors per the wide layout only).

Variants and states

sq-nav--vertical (stacked links); sq-sidebar--sticky (opt-in stickiness); hover/active via aria-current="page" (also "true"). Disabled-like nav links follow the LINKS.md pattern (aria-disabled + tabindex="-1" + explanation nearby).

Accessibility

  • Landmarks (nav + aria-label) name each navigation region —

"Primary", "Breadcrumb", "Docs" — never two unlabeled navs.

  • aria-current="page" marks the current location (CSS hooks the same

attribute — state and style cannot disagree).

  • The details toggle is keyboard-native (Enter/Space on summary);

Escape is not needed (nothing traps, nothing overlays).

  • Breadcrumb separators and pagination ellipses are CSS/text without

link semantics — screen readers hear the trail, not the slashes.

  • 44px+ targets everywhere (pagination cells are 48px).

Theme behavior

Surfaces, borders, active washes, and the current-page ring are tokens; Ocean re-skins without markup changes. Focus is the global ring in both themes.

Customization

Override --sq-nav-* tokens or restyle .sq-nav__link states in a later stylesheet. Keep current-page indication visible in every theme (wash + ring + aria-current, never color alone).

Responsive behavior

Navbars wrap; nav lists wrap; sidebars stack below 64rem; long labels wrap or scroll the page — never clipped, never squeezed. The only breakpoint-gated change is the details collapse at 48rem.

Common mistakes

  • role="menu" for site navigation — menus are for actions (OVERLAYS.md).
  • Links to the current page as clickable links — current page is text.
  • Breadcrumb separators as characters in markup ("Home / Articles") —

announced slashes are noise; CSS ::before is silent.

  • JavaScript hamburger toggles with hand-rolled aria-expanded when

details does it natively.

  • Stepper steps as clickable "skip ahead" buttons — the status display

and the navigation stay separate; a skip action is a button beside it, not step markup.

  • Steppers invented in markup without aria-current="step" — the

class alone styles but does not announce.

Tested limitations

  • No mega-menus or dropdown navigation (links + disclosure compose for

simple cases; complex cases need page CSS).

  • position: sticky sidebar needs a scrolling ancestor without

overflow: hidden (platform constraint).

  • The stepper cannot tick "done" by itself — that state is author data.
  • Single-open accordion sidebar groups are out of 1.0 scope.
